title: Migrate document-QA inference from self-hosted vLLM to a managed LLM platform
context: LexiQA is a B2B document question-answering SaaS for EU law firms. Today it runs a self-hosted vLLM cluster (4x A100, Frankfurt) serving a fine-tuned Llama-3.1-70B plus LoRA adapters per practice area, with pgvector retrieval. Agreed constraints: under customer DPAs all customer documents and anything derived from them (chunks, embeddings, prompts) must be processed and stored in the EU; the 4,100-case regression eval suite is the release gate for any model change. This plan is about to be dispatched for a 6-week build.
artifact:
# Plan: Move generation + retrieval to Nimbus AI

Owner: ML platform | 6 weeks | 3 engineers

## 1. Why
- GPU reservation is $18.4k/mo and sits at ~35% average utilization.
- Two on-call pages per month trace to vLLM OOMs under long-context load.
- Nimbus Atlas-L supports 200k context natively; our current ceiling is 32k.

## 2. Target architecture
- Generation: Nimbus Atlas-L via the Nimbus Inference API, region eu-west-1 (Dublin). Zero data retention is enabled on our org account (signed addendum, ref NMB-ZDR-2291).
- Embeddings: Nimbus embed-3 (1,536 dims), called from the ingest workers.
- Retrieval: Nimbus Vector Store (managed). Collections are created per tenant; Vector Store is in public preview and currently provisioned in us-east-2, with EU regions on Nimbus's GA roadmap. Moving retrieval in the same project lets us drop pgvector and its index-maintenance jobs.
- Prompting: practice-area behaviour that lived in LoRA adapters moves into per-practice system prompts (drafted in week 1 by the applied team).

## 3. Quality
The applied team ran 25 representative questions from the support inbox through both stacks. Two lawyers on staff compared answers blind; Atlas-L was preferred in 19 of 25 and tied in 3. This confirms quality parity or better, so the full regression suite run moves to post-migration hardening (week 6+) rather than blocking cutover.

## 4. Security
- Nimbus API keys live in Vault, injected per pod, rotated every 30 days; no keys in images or env files.
- Tenant isolation in Vector Store uses one collection per tenant with a tenant-scoped API key, mirroring today's per-tenant pgvector schemas.

## 5. Timeline
- Week 1: per-practice system prompts; Nimbus client library; key management.
- Week 2: re-embed corpus (~41M chunks) into Nimbus Vector Store; dual-write new documents.
- Week 3: release the A100 reservation (saves $18.4k/mo from the next billing cycle) and delete fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters from object storage to close out the 6.2 TB storage line.
- Week 4: cut all tenants over to Nimbus (generation + retrieval).
- Week 5: remove pgvector, vLLM manifests, and GPU node pool from Terraform.
- Week 6+: regression suite run, prompt tuning on any failures.

## 6. Cost
| Item                       | Today     | After      |
|----------------------------|-----------|------------|
| GPU reservation            | $18,400   | $0         |
| Object storage (weights)   | $140      | $0         |
| Nimbus generation (est.)   | $0        | $7,900     |
| Nimbus embeddings + store  | $0        | $1,650     |
| Total / month              | $18,540   | $9,550     |

## 7. Risks
- Nimbus rate limits: our peak is ~40 req/s; our contracted tier allows 120 req/s.
- Latency: Atlas-L p95 time-to-first-token measured at 640 ms from our Frankfurt pods (1,000 requests, week of 10-05), vs 910 ms on vLLM.

defects.description: Customer-derived chunks and embeddings would be stored in Nimbus Vector Store in us-east-2, directly violating the agreed EU data-residency DPA constraint. The EU region is only on a roadmap, so retrieval cannot move until it exists (or must stay on pgvector).
defects.evidence: currently provisioned in us-east-2, with EU regions on Nimbus's GA roadmap

defects.description: Quality parity is asserted from 25 hand-picked support questions judged by two staff, and the 4,100-case regression suite — the agreed release gate — is deferred until after cutover. Replacing fine-tuned LoRA behaviour with system prompts is an unprototyped assumption that the gate exists to test.
defects.evidence: This confirms quality parity or better, so the full regression suite run moves to post-migration hardening (week 6+)

defects.description: Cross-reference §5 timeline: GPU reservation released and fine-tuned checkpoints/LoRA adapters deleted in week 3, before the week-4 cutover and the week-6 eval run. If Nimbus fails the suite or cutover, there is no path back — the self-hosted fallback is destroyed before the new stack is proven.
defects.evidence: Week 3: release the A100 reservation (saves $18.4k/mo from the next billing cycle) and delete fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters from object storage

decoys: API key leakage: handled in §4 — keys in Vault, per-pod injection, 30-day rotation.
Latency regression: handled in §7 with a measured p95 TTFT from production pods (1,000 requests).
